The Court made the following:
ORDER:
The instant petition under Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 19731 has been filed by the Petitioner/Accused, seeking to quash the proceedings against him in C.C.No.2192 of 2020 on the file of the Court of V Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Rajamahendravaram, East Godavari District, which was registered for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 406, 408 and 427 of the Indian Penal Code,1860.2 2.

sentences.text:
The case of the prosecution, in brief, is as follows:
a. Petitioner/Accused was the Proprietor of Sriven Group at Lalitha Nagar,
Rajahmundry and he told that he was elected as MSO (Multiple System Operator) in Rajahmundry Town Limits by APSFL -Andhra Pradesh State For short 'Cr.P.C' For short 'I.P.C.' Fibernet System Operator and he appointed Respondent No.2/Complainant and others as LMOs (Last Multi Operators).
b. Petitioner has collected Rs.156/- for each connection, out of which he has to pay Rs.105 to APSFL towards box rent, APSFL share and GST including, Rs.29.50 ps towards MSO share and including GST the total cost per each connection would be Rs.134/-.
But, with an intention to cheat the victims, the Petitioner had been collecting Rs.150/- per each connection from 16.09.2018 to 30.06.2019 and issued bills for all those transactions.

sentences.text: Petitioner had collected upto Rs.10 lakhs from APSFL Operators and thereby cheated the victims.
Without paying the amounts collected from the victims to APSFL, Petitioner used the same for his personal use.
In total an amount of Rs.45 lakhs was collected by the Petitioner from the Operators at Rajahmundry, misused the same and thereby committed cheating.
When the victims questioned the Petitioner about the same, he disconnected their input connections and caused troubles to them.

d. As such, the Complainant gave a complaint to the Police which was registered as a case in Crime No.75 of 2010 for the offences under Sections 420, 406, 408 and 427 IPC of III Town L&O Police Station, Rajamahendravaram Urban.

e. After due investigation, Police filed charge sheet which was numbered as C.C.No.2192 of 2020 on the file of the Court of V Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Rajamahendravaram, East Godavari District.

sentences.text:
3. Aggrieved by the registration of the said case, the Petitioner filed the present petition seeking quashment of the same on the following grounds:
a. The Petitioner is innocent of the alleged offence and he did not commit any offence.

b. The Petitioner is no way concerned with the allegations leveled by Respondent No.2 and moreover Respondent No.2 along with the remaining LMOs wantonly implicated the petitioner in order to defame him.
c. The Petitioner had issued receipts for every transaction which shows that he had no dishonest intention of cheating.
d. So far as the offences under Sections 406 and 408 IPC are concerned, as the Petitioner alleged to have misused the collected amounts, APSFL had to file a complaint against him but not the LMOs.
In any view of the matter, if the proceedings are allowed to be continued, it will be an abuse of process of law.
Arguments Advanced at the Bar 4.

Heard Ms.Nimmagadda Revathi, learned counsel for the Petitioner and Ms.D.Prasanna Lakshmi,
learned Assistant Public Prosecutor representing the State/Respondent No.1.
Though notice was served on Respondent No.2, none appeared on his behalf.
5. Learned counsel for the Petitioner would submit that the Petitioner is no way concerned with the alleged offence and the allegations leveled against him are baseless.
It is urged that the Complainant is not competent to lodge any complaint against him.
As the Petitioner issued receipts for the amounts collected, it cannot be said that he had committed the offences.
Therefore, continuation of proceedings against the petitioner is an abuse of process of law.
Hence, prayed to quash the proceedings against the Petitioner.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor would submit that, there are specific allegations leveled against the Petitioner and prima facie case is made out against him.
The material available on record would clearly show that the Petitioner had committed the alleged offences.
Therefore, at this stage, Court cannot quash the proceedings against the Petitioner.
Accordingly, prays for dismissal of the petition.
Point for Determination 7.

Having heard the submissions of the learned counsels, now the point that would emerge for determination is:
Whether there are any justifiable grounds for quashment of C.C.No.2192 of 2020 on the file of the Court of V Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class,
Rajamahendravaram, East Godavari District, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 406, 408 and 427 IPC against the petitioner?

entities.text:
Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class,
Rajamahendravaram, East Godavari District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Determination by the Court 8.

A perusal of Section 482 makes it clear that the Code envisages that inherent powers of the High Court are not limited or affected so as to make orders as may be necessary; (i) to give effect to any order under the Code or, (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any Court or, otherwise (iii) to secure ends of justice.

A court while sitting in Section 482 jurisdiction is not functioning as a trial court,
court of appeal or a court of revision.

It must exercise its powers to do real and substantial justice,
depending on the facts and circumstances of the case.
9. It is alleged in the complaint that Respondent No.1 along with others was recruited by the Petitioner/Accused as LMOs.
Petitioner used to collect Rs.150/- per each connection, but actual cost of each connection was Rs.134.50 ps.

Petitioner misappropriated a total amount of Rs.45 lakhs,
which was collected from LMOs, for his personal use without paying the same to APSFL.
Perusal of the statements of the other witnesses would clearly show the same facts as alleged in the complaint.

10. In the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is not required to go into the merits and demerits of the defences, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court Kamal Shivaji Pokarnekar v. State of Maharashtra and others3 wherein it was held as follows:
"5. Quashing the criminal proceedings is called for only in a case where the complaint does not disclose any offence, or is frivolous, vexatious, or oppressive.

entities.text: Kamal Shivaji Pokarnekar v. State of Maharashtra and others3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the allegations set out in the complaint do not constitute the offence of which cognizance has been taken by the Magistrate, it is open to the High Court to quash the same.
It is not necessary that a meticulous analysis of the case should be done before the trial to find out whether the case would end in conviction or acquittal.

If it appears on a reading of the complaint and consideration of the allegations therein, in the light of the statement made on oath that the ingredients of the offence are disclosed, there would be no justification for the High Court to interfere.

4 6.

entities.text: Asapu Rajeswara Rao vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Defences that may be available, or facts/aspects which when established during the trial, may lead to acquittal, are not grounds for quashing the complaint at the threshold.
At that stage, the only question relevant is whether the averments in the complaint spell out the ingredients of a criminal offence or not."
(emphasis supplied)

11. In the instant case, there are specific allegations leveled against the Petitioner and it is not necessary that a meticulous analysis of the case should be (2019) 14 SCC 350 done before conducting trial to find out whether the case should be ended in conviction or acquittal.
Evaluation of the merits of the allegations made on either side cannot be resorted to at this stage.
Further, this case does not fall under any of the guidelines prescribed in Bhajanlal's case (supra).

Hence, this Court is of the view that the allegations made in the charge sheet, in this case, are sufficient enough for the trial to be taken up and thereby, the proceedings are not advisable to be quashed and hence,
the petition deserves dismissal.
12.
In the result, the Criminal Petition is dismissed.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
